title: Grok 4.20 Multi-Agent: How xAI's 4- and 16-Agent Mode Works
description: Grok 4.20 Multi-Agent runs 4 or 16 agents per query with a leader synthesizing answers. Setup, limits, billing and runnable code.
author: freellm.site
content:
Grok 4.20 Multi-Agent is a variant of xAI's Grok 4.20 that runs several agents on a single request. They work on the query in parallel, each contributing its own reasoning and tool calls, and a designated **leader agent** combines their work into the final answer you receive. You call it by sending `grok-4.20-multi-agent` to xAI's Responses API (or `x-ai/grok-4.20-multi-agent` on OpenRouter), and you choose a **4-agent** or **16-agent** setup with the `agent_count` / `reasoning.effort` parameter.

![Grok 4.20 Multi-Agent: How xAI's 4- and 16-Agent Mode Works](/images/blog/grok-4-20-multi-agent-guide/image-0.jpg)

This post draws on xAI's [multi-agent documentation](https://docs.x.ai/developers/model-capabilities/text/multi-agent), the [Grok 4.20 system card](https://data.x.ai/2026-04-07-grok-4-20-model-card.pdf), and the [OpenRouter model page](https://openrouter.ai/x-ai/grok-4.20-multi-agent). Where those sources say nothing, such as on extra benchmarks, latency figures or free-tier allowances, we tell you to check the official docs.

## What "multi-agent" means here

xAI calls the feature **Realtime Multi-agent Research**. The docs describe Grok orchestrating multiple AI agents that work together in real time on deep, multi-step research. Each agent specialises in part of the research (searching the web, analysing data, synthesising findings), and together they produce a sourced answer.

The docs list four jobs:

- **Search and gather** information from multiple sources simultaneously
- **Analyze and cross-reference** findings across different domains
- **Synthesize** a comprehensive answer with citations and supporting evidence
- **Iterate** on the research in real time, refining results from intermediate findings

The Grok 4.20 system card confirms this is a supported deployment mode and not a prompting trick: "Grok 4.20 can be deployed in two modes: single-agent (Grok 4.2 SA) or multi-agent (Grok 4.2 MA)." The card also says safety evaluations were run in both settings, with single-agent as the default reporting mode unless stated otherwise.

One design detail matters a lot in practice: **only the leader agent's output reaches you.** Sub-agent state (intermediate reasoning, tool calls and outputs) is encrypted and included only when you set `use_encrypted_content` to `True` in the xAI SDK. That keeps responses clean, and it's also how you carry the full multi-agent context across turns.

## 4 agents or 16 agents

The agent count is the setting you'll actually change, and the docs list exactly two supported values. More agents means deeper research, at the cost of more tokens and more latency.

| SDK / API | Parameter | 4 agents | 16 agents |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| xAI SDK | `agent_count` | `4` | `16` |
| OpenAI SDK | `reasoning.effort` | `"low"` or `"medium"` | `"high"` or `"xhigh"` |
| Vercel AI SDK | `reasoningEffort` | `"low"` or `"medium"` | `"high"` or `"xhigh"` |
| REST API | `reasoning.effort` | `"low"` or `"medium"` | `"high"` or `"xhigh"` |

xAI recommends 4 agents for quick research and focused queries and 16 agents for deep research on complex topics. There's no documented 8-agent or 32-agent tier. If you pass another value, check the official docs for current behaviour instead of assuming it degrades gracefully.

## How to call it (runnable)

The multi-agent variant is only available through the **Responses API**, not Chat Completions. Here's a minimal Python call using the OpenAI SDK pointed at xAI's base URL, with the 4-agent setup and two built-in tools enabled:

```python
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key=os.getenv("XAI_API_KEY"),
    base_url="https://api.x.ai/v1",
)

response = client.responses.create(
    model="grok-4.20-multi-agent",
    reasoning={"effort": "low"},          # low/medium = 4 agents, high/xhigh = 16
    input=[
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": (
                "Research the latest breakthroughs in quantum computing "
                "and summarize the key findings."
            ),
        }
    ],
    tools=[
        {"type": "web_search"},
        {"type": "x_search"},
    ],
)

print(response.output_text)
```

The same request with plain `requests`, if you'd rather not add an SDK:

```python
import os
import requests

payload = {
    "model": "grok-4.20-multi-agent",
    "reasoning": {"effort": "high"},      # 16 agents
    "input": [
        {"role": "user", "content": "Compare the top three vector databases for RAG in 2026."}
    ],
    "tools": [{"type": "web_search"}, {"type": "x_search"}],
}

r = requests.post(
    "https://api.x.ai/v1/responses",
    headers={
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
        "Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["XAI_API_KEY"],
    },
    json=payload,
    timeout=600,
)
print(r.json())
```

For streaming plus a view of reasoning progress, xAI's own SDK exposes `include=["verbose_streaming"]` and an `agent_count` parameter directly; the multi-agent docs cover that variant. Multi-turn works as it does for any other model on the Responses API: pass `previous_response_id` with a follow-up question, and the agents use the earlier context.

If you already have an OpenRouter key, the model is listed as `x-ai/grok-4.20-multi-agent`, and OpenRouter documents it against its own `/api/v1/chat/completions` endpoint with `reasoning` / `reasoning_effort` among the accepted optional fields. That conflicts with **xAI's docs, which say the multi-agent model doesn't work with the OpenAI Chat Completions API**. If you route through an aggregator and get a 400, call the Responses API on xAI directly. If this pattern is new to you, our guide to [OpenAI-compatible APIs](/blog/openai-compatible-api-guide/) explains what "drop-in" does and doesn't cover.

## Documented limitations you should plan around

xAI's docs state these outright, and three of them will break a naive integration:

- **No client-side or custom tools.** The multi-agent variant doesn't support function calling or custom tools. You get the built-in set (`web_search`, `x_search`, `code_execution`, `collections_search`) plus remote MCP tools.
- **Chat Completions API not supported.** Use the xAI SDK or the Responses API.
- **`max_tokens` is not supported.** If you used that parameter as a cost ceiling, you'll need another control: monitoring, budgets, or a hard timeout.
- **Sub-agent output is hidden by default.** If your eval harness logs intermediate chains, it will log nothing useful unless you enable encrypted content.

The docs also label the feature **beta** and warn that the API interface and behaviour may change. The parameter names above are current as of writing; re-check them before you pin them in production.

## Cost: the part that surprises people

xAI says plainly that **all tokens used by the leader agent and every sub-agent are billed**: input, output and reasoning tokens. Server-side tool calls made by any agent count toward your tool usage and are billed too.

So a single 16-agent request can use far more tokens and tool calls than one single-agent request to the same model. The response includes `usage` and `server_side_tool_usage` fields, and you should read both from day one instead of finding out what your bill looks like at the end of the month. For current per-token rates and built-in tool pricing, check [xAI's pricing page](https://docs.x.ai/developers/pricing); I'm not going to quote numbers that change weekly.

In practice, send cheap, well-scoped questions to a single-agent model and keep multi-agent for queries where cross-referencing several sources is the point. If you're comparing costs across vendors, our breakdown of [the cheapest LLM APIs after the free tier](/blog/cheapest-llm-api-after-free-tier/) shows how to compare rates without being misled by headline input prices.

## Multi-agent vs single-agent Grok 4.20: which to use

| Dimension | Grok 4.20 (single agent) | Grok 4.20 Multi-Agent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model ID | `grok-4.20` | `grok-4.20-multi-agent` |
| API surface | Chat Completions + Responses | Responses API / xAI SDK only |
| Custom function calling | Supported | Not supported |
| `max_tokens` | Supported | Not supported |
| Built-in tools | Supported | Supported (`web_search`, `x_search`, etc.) |
| Agent count control | n/a | `agent_count` 4 or 16 (`reasoning.effort`) |
| Billing | One agent's tokens | Leader **plus all sub-agents** |
| Best for | Chat, coding, tool-driven apps | Deep multi-source research, synthesis |

If your task is "answer this," use single-agent. If it's "go find out and reconcile what several sources say," that's what multi-agent mode was built for.

## Prompting it so the extra agents earn their cost

xAI's prompting guidance for this mode starts with scope: tell the agents exactly which dimensions to cover instead of asking a broad question. Sixteen agents on a vague prompt mostly get you sixteen overlapping web searches.

Name the axes ("cover pricing, rate limits, context window, and regional availability"), the sources you trust, and the output format you want. The multi-agent loop is a research loop, and the more precisely you define what "done" looks like, the less you pay for redundant tool calls.

Multi-agent systems also fail in odd ways you should know about before you ship. Coordination between agents has failure modes single models don't, including the deadlock we covered in [why two AI agents can't end a conversation](/blog/ai-agents-cant-end-conversations/). And if your agents take real actions instead of only researching, the question of who is accountable is unsettled; see [who is liable when an AI agent breaks the law](/blog/who-is-liable-when-ai-agents-break-the-law/).

## How to try it without a paid xAI account

xAI's free-tier terms change, so check our [xAI (Grok) provider page](/providers/xai/) for the current state before assuming you can test multi-agent for free. Two things to know:

1. Multi-agent requests use tokens across several agents at once, so trial credit runs out faster here than on a normal chat model.
2. Aggregators like [OpenRouter](/providers/openrouter/) list the model, which is often the easiest way to make one test call. Free-tier availability for a specific model ID is set by the aggregator, not by xAI.

If you want to prototype a research agent cheaply and switch to Grok 4.20 Multi-Agent later, start on something with a documented free allowance. Research agents use context faster than almost any other workload, so our roundups of the [best free LLM APIs in 2026](/blog/best-free-llm-apis-2026/) and [free LLM APIs with the largest context windows](/blog/free-llm-api-largest-context-window/) are good places to start.

## FAQ

### How many agents does Grok 4.20 Multi-Agent use?

There are two documented setups, 4 agents and 16 agents. You choose with `agent_count` in the xAI SDK, or with `reasoning.effort` set to `"low"`/`"medium"` (4 agents) or `"high"`/`"xhigh"` (16 agents) in the OpenAI SDK, Vercel AI SDK, or REST API.

### Can I use Grok 4.20 Multi-Agent with the OpenAI Chat Completions API?

No. xAI's docs say the multi-agent model doesn't work with the Chat Completions API; use the xAI SDK or the Responses API. OpenRouter lists the model against its own chat-completions endpoint, so behaviour through an aggregator may differ. If you get a 400, call xAI's Responses API directly.

### Does it support custom function calling?

No. The multi-agent variant doesn't support client-side or custom tools. You can use xAI's built-in tools (`web_search`, `x_search`, `code_execution`, `collections_search`) and remote MCP tools.

### How is multi-agent billed compared with single-agent?

Every token from the leader agent and all sub-agents is billed (input, output and reasoning tokens), and every server-side tool call by any agent counts toward tool usage. One multi-agent request can therefore cost far more than one single-agent request. Read `usage` and `server_side_tool_usage` in the response, and check xAI's pricing page for current rates.

### Can I see what the sub-agents did?

Only if you ask for it. By default you get the leader agent's tool calls and final response. Sub-agent reasoning, tool calls and outputs are encrypted and returned only when `use_encrypted_content` is set to `True` in the xAI SDK, and that same encrypted blob is what carries the full multi-agent context through a multi-turn conversation.
